requirements.title: Independent Dual-Station Operation
requirements.definition: The prototype must provide two mixing stations that can operate as independent beverage-mixing decks and can also be demonstrated operating together.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers station count and independent/simultaneous operation only; speed behavior, mixing output quality, and dispensing are independently testable Requirements.

requirements.title: Smooth and Frothy Matcha Mixing
requirements.definition: Each station must mix fine matcha powder into a smooth, consistent, well-aerated beverage with foam quality comparable to an effective handheld electric whisk.
requirements.boundary_note: Defines the observable beverage result; whisk construction, speed control, and splash containment are separate mechanisms that may be changed or fail independently.

requirements.title: Independent Variable-Speed Mixing Control
requirements.definition: Each station must have its own user-adjustable speed control supporting slow mixing through higher-speed frothing without requiring operation at maximum speed.
requirements.boundary_note: Motor maximum RPM, controller range, torque, and one knob per station are attributes of one speed-control mechanism rather than separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Splash-Free Mixing Operation
requirements.definition: Mixing must remain clean and controlled across the usable speed range, using whisk positioning, bowl geometry, speed limits, or a guard if required.
requirements.boundary_note: Splash containment can fail or be corrected without changing the required mixing consistency or speed-control interface.

requirements.title: Reliable Repeated and Continuous Operation
requirements.definition: The machine must tolerate repeated event use and sustained operation without overheating, excessive mechanical load, or loss of normal functionality.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers endurance and operational reliability rather than project testing activity; individual observed failures should still route to the affected atomic product Requirement.

requirements.title: Leak-Free Liquid Containment
requirements.definition: Bowls, fittings, valves, tubing, and seals must contain liquid without dripping, seeping into the enclosure, or exposing electrical components.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns seal and plumbing integrity, including the later cracked-fitting failure; controlled flow and spout appearance are separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Barista-Facing Downward Spout Geometry
requirements.definition: The custom spouts must face the barista, resemble the rendered design as closely as practical, and direct the beverage downward into cups rather than along a flat or extended path.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers outlet location, direction, custom shape, and render correspondence; valve actuation, leak integrity, and cleanability are independently testable.

requirements.title: Compact Matcha Bowl Capacity and Form
requirements.definition: The machine must use relatively small, deep bowls consistent with the earlier visual concept to favor mixing quality, foam consistency, rapid event cycles, and compact proportions.
requirements.boundary_note: Bowl capacity, depth, and visual scale are attributes of one vessel choice; rapid removal and sanitation are separate behaviors.

requirements.title: Quick Bowl Removal and Swapping
requirements.definition: Each bowl must lift out easily and support rapid swapping during events without obstruction from the whisk, motor tower, or plumbing connection.
requirements.boundary_note: Operational bowl exchange has its own clearance and quick-release behavior and can be modified separately from bowl capacity or general sanitation.

requirements.title: Cleanable and Sanitary Food Path
requirements.definition: Bowls, whisks, spouts, valves, and plumbing that contact matcha or milk must be removable, flushable, or otherwise accessible enough for reliable cleaning without hidden liquid traps.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers sanitation access and removal of food-contact components; material composition and non-food-contact maintenance access are separate Requirements.

requirements.title: Food-Safe Contact Materials
requirements.definition: All liquid and beverage contact areas must use appropriate food-safe materials such as stainless steel, food-grade silicone, or suitable food-grade plastics.
requirements.boundary_note: Material safety is independently assessable from whether the same components are easy to remove or clean.

requirements.title: 120V Wall-Powered Electrical System
requirements.definition: The V1 prototype must operate from a standard 120V wall outlet through a properly rated low-voltage supply and motor controllers with sufficient capacity for both motors, valves, and cooling loads.
requirements.boundary_note: Input source, converted voltage, current capacity, and overload margin are attributes of one V1 power architecture; the user-facing master switch is separate.

requirements.title: Dedicated Master Power Control
requirements.definition: The machine must provide a functional, accessible master power button or switch rather than relying solely on plugging and unplugging the wall cord.
requirements.boundary_note: Owns power activation and shutdown behavior; button lighting and decorative styling belong to visual Requirements.

requirements.title: Compact Functional Enclosure
requirements.definition: The enclosure must house the motors, valves, piping, controls, and deep bowls while remaining reasonably compact and preserving practical event-use proportions.
requirements.boundary_note: Enclosure thickness, equipment fit, and accepted bulk are attributes of one packaging constraint; appearance, raised cup platform, and service access can change separately.

requirements.title: Stable and Vibration-Resistant Structure
requirements.definition: The assembled machine and motor towers must remain sturdy and stable during operation without rattling, walking, or excessive structural vibration.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers physical rigidity and motion under load; acoustic noise, endurance, and splash behavior are separately testable.

requirements.title: Accessible Internal Components
requirements.definition: Panels, motor towers, electronics, and plumbing must be accessible for future inspection, adjustment, repair, or replacement.
requirements.boundary_note: Maintenance access to non-food-contact internals is distinct from routine sanitation and removal of bowls, whisks, or spouts.

requirements.title: Acceptable Event-Environment Noise
requirements.definition: The operating mixer should not produce excessive motor, drivetrain, fan, or vibration noise for use at live events.
requirements.boundary_note: Noise is an independently observable acceptance behavior and should not be merged with structural stability merely because vibration can contribute to it.

requirements.title: Beige and Green Color Scheme
requirements.definition: The mixer and platform must use the client-selected beige-dominant palette with coordinated green accents and matching text or marking colors.
requirements.boundary_note: Color palette can be changed independently from logos, labels, LED behavior, or DJ-style decorative controls.

requirements.title: DJ-Turntable Visual Details
requirements.definition: The visible machine and platform should evoke the supplied DJ-turntable renderings through details such as deck labels, silver or faux controls, bowl measurement rings, and other turntable-like design cues.
requirements.boundary_note: Groups concrete turntable-inspired decorative elements as one visual language; functional speed/dispense controls, branding text, and active lighting retain independent lifecycles.

requirements.title: LED Accent Lighting
requirements.definition: The design should include suitable LED accent lighting, particularly around the bowls or power control, to make the machine visually engaging for events and social media.
requirements.boundary_note: Lighting requires its own components and placement decisions and can be deferred or implemented without changing static colors, labels, or functional controls.

requirements.title: CAD and System Layout Drawings
requirements.definition: The project must produce CAD or equivalent design drawings showing the system layout, enclosure, component placement, and refined dimensions.
requirements.boundary_note: CAD/layout is an independently requested executable artifact; it should not be merged with the BOM or electrical wiring plan.

requirements.title: Prototype Bill of Materials
requirements.definition: The project must provide and maintain a component-level bill of materials reflecting the approved prototype design and selected compatible parts.
requirements.boundary_note: The BOM is a standalone deliverable with its own revisions and approval; purchasing and reimbursement administration are excluded.

requirements.title: Electrical Wiring Plan
requirements.definition: The project must provide a basic wiring overview or plan documenting the electrical interconnection of the supply, motor controllers, motors, valves, fans, and controls.
requirements.boundary_note: The wiring plan is an independently useful artifact and does not own the runtime correctness of the power system or controls.

requirements.title: Off-the-Shelf V1 Component Strategy
requirements.definition: The first prototype should use simple, cost-effective, readily available components where practical while allowing custom fabrication where required for core behavior or appearance.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a V1 implementation constraint rather than a generic cost or schedule requirement; custom spouts and enclosure parts are permissible exceptions where off-the-shelf parts cannot satisfy the behavior.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Larry — I went through the BOM and overall I really like the direction. This is exactly what I was hoping for.

A few thoughts I’d like your input on before we move forward:

• Motors — I’m wondering if 200 RPM might be a bit low for achieving a strong, frothy matcha texture. Do you think it makes sense to increase RPM while still maintaining enough torque for smooth mixing?

• Whisk — would a stainless steel or milk-frother-style head perform better than the resin whisk in terms of consistency, durability, and foam quality?

• Spout — I’d like to stick with the solenoid approach. It’s important that the pour is clean, controlled, and seamless (mix → open → pour) both for texture and the overall visual experience.

• Splash / mess control — this is really important for events. I want to make sure:
– minimal to no splashing during mixing
– smooth, controlled flow from the spout (no sputtering)
– no dripping when the valve is closed
– good sealing so nothing leaks into the base
– some form of splash guard or lip around the bowl if needed

• Cleaning — I’d like the bowls and spout components to be easy to clean or removable if possible.

Everything else looks great to me. Curious to hear your thoughts on these and if you’d adjust anything before we finalize the BOM.

value_updates.desired_mixing_result: strong, frothy matcha texture with smooth mixing, consistent results, and good foam quality

source_message.speaker: client

One thing I do want to make sure of with the higher RPM:
• we keep splashing under control
• the mixing stays smooth and doesn’t get too aggressive at higher speeds

So if needed, I’m open to adding a splash guard or dialing in whisk position / bowl depth to make sure it performs cleanly.

Overall I’m good with this direction.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Larry — I went through the finalized BOM and everything is looking really solid. I like the direction a lot and I think we’re very close to locking this in.

I just had a few quick things I wanted to confirm before I move forward with ordering parts:

• Motors — I noticed the listing mentions an eccentric output shaft. Just want to confirm that this will still give us a smooth, centered rotation for the whisk, or if we should consider a straight/centered shaft for better stability.

• Motor performance — I like the move to 3000 RPM for flexibility. I just want to make sure we’ll be able to dial it in for smooth mixing and avoid overly aggressive splashing at higher speeds.

• Solenoid flow — since we’re using on/off valves, do you expect the pour to be smooth when opening, or will it release too abruptly? I want to make sure we get a clean, controlled pour without splashing.

• Power supply — with both motors, solenoids, and fans running, are we comfortably within the limits of the 12V 20A power supply under load?

• Splash control — with the higher RPM, I just want to confirm that whisk positioning, bowl depth, and overall layout will keep things clean during operation. I want this to be as splash-proof and mess-free as possible for events.

Everything else looks great to me — just want to make sure we’re fully dialed in on these before the order is placed.

Let me know your thoughts.

A few thoughts I’d like your input on before we move forward:

• Motors — I’m wondering if 200 RPM might be a bit low for achieving a strong, frothy matcha texture. Do you think it makes sense to increase RPM while still maintaining enough torque for smooth mixing?

• Whisk — would a stainless steel or milk-frother-style head perform better than the resin whisk in terms of consistency, durability, and foam quality?

• Splash / mess control — this is really important for events. I want to make sure:
– minimal to no splashing during mixing
– smooth, controlled flow from the spout (no sputtering)
– no dripping when the valve is closed
– good sealing so nothing leaks into the base
– some form of splash guard or lip around the bowl if needed

• Cleaning — I’d like the bowls and spout components to be easy to clean or removable if possible.

Everything else looks great to me. Curious to hear your thoughts on these and if you’d adjust anything before we finalize the BOM.

Hi Larry,

Thank you for the update.

After reviewing our original project discussions and scope, I understand that the initial focus was primarily on the engineering, wiring, circuitry, prototyping, and functionality of the machine. As the project evolved, I became more focused on the aesthetic and branding aspects, but I can see how the original scope was centered more heavily on developing a functional prototype.

My primary concern at this point is ensuring that the machine is mechanically sound, reliable, and operates as intended. Functionality and performance are my highest priorities.

I would like to see the demonstration of the prototype as soon as it is available. Please include the machine operating under normal use conditions so I can evaluate the mixing performance, stability, and overall functionality.

Once I receive and review the demonstration, I would like to move forward with completing the remaining wiring, enclosure fabrication, and base fabrication so that the machine can be shipped.

Regarding aesthetics, I appreciate your willingness to incorporate the "K" button markings and discuss lighting options. I will likely pursue additional branding, industrial design, and cosmetic refinements separately after receiving the prototype, so my immediate focus is on getting a fully functioning machine completed and delivered.

Please provide the demonstration and an updated target ship date once the remaining work is complete.
